title: wb pickup records the session id only when --session is passed, so a node's header names a dead session
body:
`intent wb pickup` writes a node's `session_id` only when `--session` is passed: `pick_up` in `intentsvcs/src/store.rs` keeps the row's value through `coalesce(?3, session_id)` when the flag is absent, and the `/in-whiteboard` skill's pickup line passes no `--session`. A node that boots by the skill therefore keeps whatever id an earlier session last wrote, and nothing reports it.

Measured 2026-09-17 at boot, from `intent wb status --json` against the transcripts under `~/.claude/projects/-Users-matts-Devel-prj-Intent/`: all four Claude nodes' headers named sessions that had ended. cc's header named `e3744ab1` where its previous session's transcript was `7899f335`, and ic's named `7f9cf959` where its previous was `7a8a2358`, so both were older than the node's last session. dc's named its previous session, `effb6a8d`. vc's named `bc2638fd` and was corrected by hand with `--session`.

Why it matters: the validation method finds a node's transcript from the `session_id` on its header, to check what was asked against what was built. A header naming a dead session sends that read to the wrong transcript, and nothing distinguishes the wrong transcript from the right one.

The fix (hv, 2026-09-17, first-hand, into the close-out): when `--session` is absent, `wb pickup` takes the id from `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`; an explicit flag still wins; with neither, the row keeps its value as today. The environment is read at the CLI edge and the store call is unchanged. One arm: a pickup with the variable set and no flag records it on the node's header. The builder says in the landing whether the MCP pickup tool's process carries the variable, and gives it the same default if it does. Size XS.


**CLOSED 2026-09-17, by the landing at d8055887f, on vc's word.** `wb pickup` with no `--session` now records the session it runs in. `render::pickup_session` takes the flag when one is passed, else a non-empty `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, else nothing, and with nothing the row keeps its value as it did. The environment is read at the CLI edge, and the store call is unchanged.

**The MCP pickup tool takes the same default, because its process carries the variable.** Measured at the fix: every `intent mcp` process on this machine held its own session's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and the tool calls the same function rather than reading the variable itself.

The shipped surface's environment guard, `no_intent_home.rs`, now allows the variable on hv's ruling in this issue and confines it to `render.rs`, the precedent `VISUAL` and `EDITOR` set. The `--session` flag's help says what it defaults to.

Guarded by `a_pickup_with_no_session_flag_records_the_session_it_runs_in` in `wb_pickup_records_the_session_it_runs_in.rs`. The arm removes the variable from every other call, so a run inside a Claude Code session cannot lend the fixture its id. It was red on the base, where the header's `session_id` was null, and green on the fix. The judging run on the bank was green: the whole intentsvcs, intent-cli and intentd suites, workspace clippy and rustfmt.

The fix is live for a pickup once the installed pair is rebuilt past d8055887f.
